open_questions: Live Online Sunshine statute pages (flsenate.gov) timed out on every fetch attempt (3 tries), so the exact current subsection placement of the owner/operator ad license-number rule within s. 509.241(3) was confirmed only via the official SB 280 final staff analysis, not the live codified text. Re-verify the current numbering against the live page before publishing.

The DBPR vacation-rental/timeshare licensing guide page (formerly www2.myfloridalicense.com/hotelsrestaurants/licensing/vrtspguide/) now redirects to the generic MyFloridaLicense.com landing page; the current online application path for VR licenses and whether DBPR still accepts the mail-in HR-7028 packet could not be confirmed from an official page.

Whether the vacation rental information system (s. 509.244) is live and where advertising platforms access it — the 1/1/2026 platform verification duty is now in effect, but no official DBPR system page or API documentation was found.
The staggered renewal schedule detail (R. 61C-1.006 county-based expiration dates) could not be verified; annual renewal is statutory, but the specific month/day per county remains unverified.

Fee confirmation: the fee figures come from the 61C-1.008 proposed-rule text (2011-era, corroborated by the 2024 SB 280 staff analysis). No later rulemaking reducing/increasing lodging fees was found, but the current adopted rule text on flrules.org should be checked directly for any post-2011 amendments before quoting fees externally.

requirements.agency: DBPR, Division of Hotels and Restaurants
requirements.applies_when: You rent a Florida property to transient guests more than three times in a calendar year for periods of less than 30 days or 1 calendar month, whichever is less — i.e., it is a 'vacation rental' as defined in Fla. Stat. s. 509.242(1)(c) and a transient public lodging establishment under Fla. Stat. s. 509.013(4)(a)1
requirements.notes: Vacation rental = any unit or group of units in a condominium or cooperative, or any individually or collectively owned single-family, two-family, three-family, or four-family house or dwelling unit, that is also a transient public lodging establishment but not a timeshare project (per HR-7028 packet, quoting 509.242(1)(c)). Threshold: rented to guests more than 3 times/calendar year for <30 days or 1 calendar month (DBPR guide definition of transient public lodging establishment).
requirements.timeline: must apply for and receive the license BEFORE commencing operation; operating without a license is a misdemeanor of the second degree
requirements.title: DBPR Division of Hotels and Restaurants vacation rental license required before operation

requirements.agency: DBPR, Division of Hotels and Restaurants
requirements.applies_when: Choosing the license category on form DBPR HR-7028: a unit or group of units in a condominium or cooperative gets the Condominium license (code 2006); a single-family house, townhouse, or unit/group of units in a duplex, triplex, quadruplex, or other dwelling of four or fewer units gets the Dwelling license (code 2007)
requirements.citation: Fla. Stat. s. 509.242(1)(c), (g); R. 61C-1.002, F.A.C. (definitions incorporated in HR-7028)

forms.name: DBPR HR-7028, Application for Vacation Rental or Timeshare Project License

requirements.notes: Distinct from hotels/motels and other transient public lodging classifications licensed on DBPR HR-7027 (round-1 restaurant work shares only the division and fee-rule family, not these classifications — recorded here only as the category map). If 25% or more of the units in a public lodging establishment fall within a different classification than the establishment is licensed under, a separate license is required (s. 509.242(2)).
requirements.title: Vacation rental license type: Condominium vs Dwelling (vs Timeshare Project)

requirements.agency: DBPR, Division of Hotels and Restaurants
requirements.applies_when: One owner with one unit/dwelling = Single; a licensed agent covering all vacation-rental units within a building or group of buildings in a single complex = Group; a licensed agent covering houses/units at separate locations = Collective (max 75 houses/units per license, restricted to counties within one district)
requirements.citation: R. 61C-1.002(4), F.A.C. (as quoted in HR-7028 packet)
requirements.fees: fee varies by class and unit count (see 61C-1.008)

forms.name: DBPR HR-7028, Application for Vacation Rental or Timeshare Project License

requirements.notes: Single licenses are issued to the individual owner/entity (owner responsible for sanitation/safety violations); Group and Collective licenses are issued to a 'licensed agent' (management company) who is responsible for violations.
requirements.title: Vacation rental license classifications: Single, Group, Collective

requirements.agency: DBPR, Division of Hotels and Restaurants
requirements.applies_when: Applying for a new vacation rental license or a change of ownership on DBPR HR-7028
requirements.fees: $50 one-time application processing fee in addition to the license fee (check/money order; no cash)

forms.name: DBPR HR-7028, Application for Vacation Rental or Timeshare Project License (signed under oath per s. 559.79(2))
DBPR HR-7020, Certificate of Balcony Inspection (required if establishment is 3 or more stories; certifies balconies/platforms/stairways/railings inspected by competent person)

requirements.notes: Packet requires: Florida sales tax number (or exemption), FEIN (business/corporate) or SSN/ITIN, a list of ALL units to be licensed (s. 509.241 requires licensed agent/operator to notify the division of all units), completed balcony-inspection certificate for buildings 3+ stories (reinspection every 3 years; form expires 3 years from inspection date), and the $50 application processing fee. Online filing is also referenced via www.MyFloridaLicense.com/dbpr/hr, but the packet text is mail-in.
requirements.timeline: mail completed packet to Division of Hotels and Restaurants, 2601 Blair Stone Road, Tallahassee, FL 32399-0783; allow up to 30 days for processing after mailing
requirements.title: Vacation rental license application requirements

requirements.agency: DBPR, Division of Hotels and Restaurants
requirements.applies_when: Initial license application and each annual renewal of a vacation rental license
requirements.fees: Group/Single: 1 unit $170; 2-25 units $180; 26-50 $195; 51-100 $210; 101-200 $235; 201-300 $265; 301-400 $295; 401-500 $320; over 500 $350 (each = basic $150 + incremental fee + $10 HEP). Collective: $150 basic + $10 per unit + $10 HEP (varies). Plus $50 one-time application processing fee on initial/change-of-ownership applications. Delinquency: $50 if renewal filed within 30 days after expiration; $100 if filed 31-60 days after. Initial applicants pay the full license fee if applying during or more than 6 months before the annual renewal period; half fee if 6 months or less before. The $10 HEP fee is payable in full regardless of timing.
requirements.notes: Fees are based on number of rental units; aggregate per-establishment cap is $1,000 (app/delinquency fees excluded from cap per s. 509.251). Renewal fees are based on the number of units under license at the time of the renewal period (unless timely addition/deletion notice given per 61C-1.002(4)(c)5.c.). HEP = Hospitality Education Program fee per s. 509.302 (capped at $10/establishment).
requirements.timeline: fees due before license is issued or renewed
requirements.title: Vacation rental license fee schedule (61C-1.008)

requirements.agency: DBPR, Division of Hotels and Restaurants
requirements.applies_when: All licensed vacation rentals and timeshare projects

forms.name: DBPR HR-7020, Certificate of Balcony Inspection (for 3+ story buildings, inspected by a competent inspector; reinspection every 3 years)

requirements.notes: HR-7028 packet states verbatim: 'We do not require inspections prior to licensing vacation rentals or timeshare projects, but we may inspect at any time upon request or complaint.' s. 509.032(2)(a) requires biannual inspections of each licensed public lodging establishment EXCEPT that 'public lodging units classified as vacation rentals or timeshare projects are not subject to this requirement but shall be made available to the division upon request.' Local-government building-code and fire-code inspections (ss. 553.80, 633.206) are NOT preempted. Balcony certification is the one affirmative inspection-like requirement at application (buildings 3+ stories).
requirements.timeline: balcony certificates valid 3 years; division may inspect vacation rentals at any time upon request or complaint
requirements.title: Inspection rules for vacation rentals: no pre-licensing inspection; no routine biannual inspections

requirements.agency: DBPR, Division of Hotels and Restaurants
requirements.applies_when: Every licensed establishment; the vacation-rental-specific rule applies once the property is licensed and, if applicable, locally registered
requirements.citation: Fla. Stat. s. 509.241(3), as amended by Ch. 2024-239 (SB 280), effective 1/1/2025
requirements.notes: Any license issued by the division must be conspicuously displayed to the public inside the office or lobby of the licensed establishment. SB 280 added: the vacation rental's local registration number, if applicable, must be conspicuously displayed inside the vacation rental. The division must also assign a unique identifier on each vacation rental license identifying each individual vacation rental dwelling or unit (s. 509.241(5), eff. 1/1/2025).
requirements.title: Display of license and registration information in/on the vacation rental

requirements.agency: DBPR, Division of Hotels and Restaurants
requirements.applies_when: The owner or operator of a vacation rental offered for transient occupancy through an advertising platform places an advertisement or listing for the rental
requirements.citation: Fla. Stat. s. 509.241(3), as amended by Ch. 2024-239 (SB 280)
requirements.notes: Per the official SB 280 final bill analysis: the owner or operator must include the property's vacation rental license number with the associated unique identifier issued by the division and, if applicable, the local registration number on the vacation rental's advertisement, and attest that, to the best of their knowledge, those numbers are current, valid, and accurate. The owner/operator must also display the local registration and licensure information inside the vacation rental property. Note: the earlier 2023 bill (SB 714, which died) contained a similar owner-ad rule; the enacted rule is the SB 280 version. Exact current subsection placement could not be re-verified against the live Online Sunshine page (fetch timed out) — see open questions.
requirements.title: Owner/operator must display vacation rental license number (with unique identifier) in advertisements

requirements.agency: DBPR, Division of Hotels and Restaurants (platform duty); platforms: Airbnb/VRBO-type 'advertising platforms'
requirements.applies_when: Any advertising platform publishing a vacation rental advertisement or listing for rent in Florida
requirements.citation: Fla. Stat. ss. 509.243, 509.244 (created by Ch. 2024-239, SB 280)
requirements.notes: Per enrolled SB 280 text: (1) platform must require the ad placer to (a) include the vacation rental license number with the associated unique identifier and, if applicable, the local registration number, and (b) attest the numbers are current, valid, and accurately stated; (2) the platform must display the license number with unique identifier and local registration number; (3) effective 1/1/2026 the platform must use the vacation rental information system (s. 509.244, created by the same bill and maintained by the division) to verify the license number + unique identifier and local registration number are current, valid, and apply to the subject rental BEFORE publishing — it may not advertise a rental that fails to provide a valid number and must remove non-compliant listings from public view. The regulation of advertising platforms is preempted to the state (s. 509.032). The division also collects/uses the system to let advertising platforms search by and verify license numbers and local registration numbers.
requirements.timeline: core duties effective 1/1/2025; verification-before-publishing duties effective 1/1/2026
requirements.title: Advertising platforms must collect, attest, and display vacation rental license numbers — and (since 1/1/2026) verify them against the state system before publishing

requirements.agency: DBPR, Division of Hotels and Restaurants
requirements.applies_when: Every vacation rental licensee; renewal each year; licensed agents must keep an online account with the division
requirements.fees: renewal fee per 61C-1.008 schedule based on units under license; $50 delinquency (within 30 days after expiration), $100 (31-60 days after)
requirements.notes: s. 509.241(1): licenses shall be renewed annually, division adopts a rule establishing a staggered schedule for license renewals. s. 509.241(4) (added by SB 280): each person planning to open a public lodging establishment and each licensee or licensed agent must create and maintain a division online account and provide an email address as the primary contact; each vacation rental operator must submit any applicable local vacation rental registration number through the division's online system within 5 days after registration. Exact county-based stagger dates (R. 61C-1.006) were not verified — see open questions.
requirements.timeline: licenses renewed annually on a staggered schedule set by rule
requirements.title: Annual renewal, staggered schedule, and division online account

requirements.agency: DBPR, Division of Hotels and Restaurants
requirements.applies_when: Sale/transfer of a licensed vacation rental property; any new applicant wanting to operate before final agency action
requirements.citation: Fla. Stat. s. 509.241(1)-(2), as amended by Ch. 2024-239 (SB 280), effective 1/1/2025

forms.name: DBPR HR-7028 (select 'Change of Ownership' application type; attach previous operator's valid, date-stamped Certificate of Balcony Inspection under HR-7020 Section 3)

requirements.notes: Licenses 'may not be transferred from one place or individual to another' (s. 509.241(1)); HR-7028 has a 'Change of Ownership (previously licensed within the last year by H&R)' application type. Effective 1/1/2025, upon receiving a vacation rental license application the division may grant a temporary license authorizing the vacation rental to begin operation while the application is pending and to post the information required under s. 509.243(1)(c); it expires automatically on final agency action.
requirements.timeline: temporary license granted upon receipt of application; automatically expires upon final agency action
requirements.title: License is non-transferable; change of ownership requires a new application; temporary license available while pending

requirements.agency: DBPR, Division of Hotels and Restaurants
requirements.applies_when: A licensed vacation rental violates a condo/co-op/HOA lease or property restriction (per final court order or arbitrator's written decision), or its local registration is suspended/revoked, or the premises/owner is subject to a final order directing termination of the vacation-rental use
requirements.citation: Fla. Stat. s. 509.241 (discipline provisions added by Ch. 2024-239, SB 280), s. 509.244
requirements.notes: When revoking, suspending, or refusing to renew, the division must specify the license number with the associated unique identifier of the dwelling/unit affected and input the status into the vacation rental information system (s. 509.244).
requirements.timeline: division may suspend up to 30 days or revoke/refuse to issue or renew; a suspension based on local registration suspension must run concurrently with the local suspension
requirements.title: Division discipline of vacation rental licenses (suspension/revocation tied to local registration and association orders)

requirements.agency: Local governments, under state framework (Fla. Stat. s. 509.032(8), as amended by Ch. 2024-239)
requirements.applies_when: Any Florida vacation rental in a jurisdiction that has adopted a local registration ordinance — separate from and in addition to the state DBPR license
requirements.fees: state cap: local government may charge no more than $150 per unit for processing a registration application and no more than $50 per unit for annual renewal processing (Ch. 2024-239 figures; earlier bills used $100/$200 thresholds)
requirements.notes: State law preempts regulation of public lodging establishments to the state (sanitation, inspections, personnel training) and preempts local laws that prohibit vacation rentals or regulate the duration/frequency of rental (s. 509.032(7)(b)) — localities may still enforce building and fire codes. s. 509.032(8) as amended by SB 280 authorizes (does not require) local vacation-rental registration programs with the fee caps above. Local registration is the subject of a separate local-layer round; included here only as the state statutory context that shapes the state license (e.g., the 5-day local-reg-number reporting duty).
requirements.timeline: local registration may require annual renewal at most once per year; operator must submit the local registration number to the division within 5 days of registration (s. 509.241(4)(c))
requirements.title: State framework for local vacation rental registration (state law context for the state license)
